Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

excite verb

stir up feelings, rouse

also stir up, rouse, arouse, fire up, excite interest, excitement

classical

Cic. Fam. 3.11.3: quōs ego rīsūs excitāssem!
Traupman 152

excitō, excitāre, excitāvī, excitātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

rouse, stir up, call forth (a feeling, laughter, interest)

Its first sense is to wake someone or call him out (ē somnō excitāre); from there, to rouse a person to effort or to call forth a feeling, laughter or a fire (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s word for “excite”.

Other words

  • concitō, concitāre, concitāvī, concitātum — stir up, rouse, work up (a crowd, a person, a passion)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive: the person with ad or in · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.204 (Lewis & Short): concitārī ad studium cognōscendae percipiendaeque virtūtis

    Stronger than excitāre: to set in violent motion, a horse with the spurs, a crowd to arms, a mind to anger or zeal (Lewis & Short). Concitātus is “agitated, worked up”.

  • incendō, incendere, incendī, incēnsum — fire up, inflame

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.4: omnēsque incenduntur ad studia glōriā

    Literally “set on fire”; of the mind, to fire with zeal, love or anger.

  • animī commōtiō, animī commōtiōnis f. — excitement, emotion

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.8 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152

    The noun for “excitement”: a stirring of the mind (Lewis & Short, s.v. commōtiō). See also affect, for being moved.

Examples

  • mihi ille dētur puer, quem laus excitet, quem glōria juvet, quī victus fleat

    give me the boy whom praise fires up, who loves glory, who cries when he losesQuīnt. 1.3.7

  • honōs alit artēs, omnēsque incenduntur ad studia glōriā

    honour feeds the arts, and everyone is fired to effort by gloryCic. Tusc. 1.4

  • mē miserum, quī nōn adfuerim! quōs ego rīsūs excitāssem!

    too bad I wasn’t there! what laughs I’d have raised!Cic. Fam. 3.11.3

See also excited, affect, emotion.
